column2: Layer sauce, lasagne sheets, béchamel and cheese in a baking dish; repeat for 3 layers.
Cover with foil and bake at 180 °C for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and brown for another 10 minutes; rest for 15 minutes.
Resting keeps the slices from falling apart.
Creamy mushroom chicken (stroganoff style)
1 cup cream
1 tablespoon mustard
Cut the chicken into strips and sear in butter.
Add the onion and mushrooms and sauté for 7 minutes.
Add the pepper and mustard.
Add the cream and cook over low heat for 8 minutes.
Serve with rice or pasta.
Mustard gives the sauce depth.
Shakshuka (eggs in pepper sauce)
400 g tomatoes
1 dessert spoon cumin, sweet paprika, salt
Fry the onion and pepper in oil for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until thickened.
Make hollows in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cook covered for 5–6 minutes and serve with parsley.
Leave the eggs to the consistency you like.
Hot, with bread.
Teriyaki salmon
2 salmon fillets
Mix the soy sauce, honey, ginger, garlic and cornflour with 3 tablespoons water.
Cook the salmon skin side down in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes.
Turn and cook for 3 more minutes.
Add the sauce and spoon it over the salmon until thickened.
Sprinkle with sesame and serve with rice.
Cornflour makes the sauce glossy and thick.
Same day.
Gnocchi (potato)
500 g floury potatoes
For the sauce: 3 tablespoons butter and a few sage leaves
Boil the potatoes in their skins, peel while hot and mash.
Make a soft dough with the flour, egg yolk and salt; don’t overwork it.
Roll the dough into finger-thick ropes and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Cook in boiling salted water; once they float, cook 1 minute more and remove.
Toss in butter with the sage and serve.
Too much flour makes the gnocchi tough.
With parmesan.
Uncooked gnocchi can be frozen.
Indian-style chickpea curry (chana masala)
Fry the onion in oil for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and 1 glass of water and cook for 15 minutes.
Serve with coriander or parsley.
Frying the spices in oil releases their aroma.
Quesadilla (cheese and chicken)
2 tortillas
150 g boiled, shredded chicken
Half a cup sweetcorn
1 red pepper (finely diced)
Spread the cheese, chicken, corn and pepper over half the tortilla.
Fold over.
Toast in a dry pan for 3–4 minutes on each side.
The cheese should melt.
Cut into triangles.
A dry pan gives crispness.
With a yogurt sauce.
Paella-style chicken rice
300 g chicken thighs
3 cups hot chicken stock
Brown the chicken in a wide pan and remove.
Cook the onion, pepper and tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and turmeric and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken stock, peas and chicken and cook for 20 minutes without stirring.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.
Don’t stir; let a lightly crisp layer form on the bottom.
Greek salad (horiatiki)
150 g white cheese (sliced)
Half a cup black olives
Cut the tomatoes into large chunks and the cucumber into half-moons.
Slice the pepper and onion into rings.
Put the vegetables in a bowl.
Add the olives and place the cheese on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with oregano.
Leave the cheese whole as a slice, without crumbling it.
Tom yum-style chicken soup
1 stalk lemongrass or 1 lemon peel
5 cups chicken stock
Boil the chicken stock with the ginger and lemongrass for 5 minutes.
Add the thinly sliced chicken and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, lemon juice and chilli flakes.
Add the lemon juice last.
Pad thai-style chicken noodles
250 g rice noodles
1 cup bean sprouts or julienned carrot
1 tablespoon brown sugar
3 tablespoons peanuts (crushed)
Soften the noodles in lukewarm water according to the packet instructions.
Cut the chicken into strips, cook in a hot pan and push to one side.
Crack the eggs into the pan and scramble them.
Add the noodles, vegetables, soy sauce and sugar and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Serve with spring onions, lime and peanuts.
If there is a peanut allergy, leave out the peanuts.
Oven-baked chicken breast with vegetables (no added fat)
4 chicken breasts
Rub the chicken with lemon, thyme and salt.
Coarsely chop the vegetables and toss with oil.
Arrange the chicken and vegetables on the tray.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the inside of the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Flattening the chicken breast helps it cook evenly.
Lentil and quinoa patties
1 cup cooked quinoa
1 cup cooked green lentils
Roughly mash the lentils with a fork.
Knead all the ingredients together.
Shape into patties and arrange on a lined tray.
If the mixture falls apart, add 1 more spoon of oats.
Chia pudding (with fruit)
4 tablespoons chia seeds
Half a cup fruit
Mix the chia, milk, honey and cinnamon.
Stir again after 5 minutes to prevent clumping.
Leave in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Divide between bowls.
